- Type designations: IT4000E[T], IT6000E[T], IT8000E[T], IT3000M, IT2000M
- Module designation: not applicable? Not mentioned. The characteristics say specs depend on modules used. I'll leave module_designation null or omit.
- Description: Non-automatic weighing instrument

Model family: 5 type designations, but no attribute matrix per model — characteristics "depend on the modules used". The table says Maximum capacity, Verification scale interval, Weighing range(s), Software identification — all with a note that these depend on modules used and compatibility checked via R 76 annex F. So no concrete values. Should I create model_family with the 5 models? The schema says include model_family ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. The cert does cover 5 types. But there are no per-model attributes. I could list the models with just model_id. That seems reasonable.

Actually, the characteristics values are not numeric — they're a textual note. Per rule "Don't fabricate" — I shouldn't invent values. I could add a type_level characteristic "maximum_capacity" with value as string? No — the cell is a note, not a value. Better to omit numeric characteristics, but record the note as description or in matrix_tables? Hmm.

I think best: model_family with the 5 model_ids (since types vary), and characteristics omitted (no concrete values). Maybe record the note as a description field on certified_type or a footnote. There are no numbered footnotes.

Recommendation:
- R 76-1:2006 → id "R76", edition 2006, part? The schema says edition (int). R76-1:2006 — edition 2006. accuracy_classes: ["III", "IIII"]. Scheme A.

Role: these are "reports" listed as tests and examinations — the certificate says "the associated reports". I'll use "test_report" or "type_evaluation_report". Since R76 scheme A requires Type Evaluation Report, the first is likely the TER. But we don't know roles per report; safest is "test_report" for all, or "type_evaluation_report"? The certificate says "conformity was established by the results of tests and examinations provided in the associated reports". I'll use "test_report" for all.

Revision history:
- revision "0", date 2024-05-21, changes "Initial issue."

Characteristics: Accuracy class (III) or (IIII) — type_level characteristic accuracy_class with value "(III) or (IIII)"? Better: recommendation.accuracy_classes = ["III", "IIII"]. Also characteristics.type_level accuracy_class value string "III or IIII"? Structured values must be object with value/unit. I could do:
"accuracy_class": {"value": ["III", "IIII"], ...} — hmm, list of values. The rules say lists of numeric values → model matrix. Here it's accuracy classes, which go in recommendation. I'll add type_level: {"accuracy_class": {"value": "III or IIII", "unit_symbol": null}}. Or omit. I think including it as a string value is fine.

Note about load cells: "Other load cells than the types listed in the reports above may be used provided there is an OIML Certificate of Conformity (R 60)..." — could be a note/description. I'll include in certified_type.description or as a footnote-like note. Maybe add to description.

Certificate number: "R76/2006-A-NL1-24.16" — include revision 0? The schema certificate has number; revision is in revision_history. Number field: "R76/2006-A-NL1-24.16".

Date issued: 2024-05-21.

The characteristics table note: "These specifications depend on the modules used. The compatibility of the modules shall be checked using R 76 (2006) annex F..." — I'll include this as certified_type.description supplement or as matrix_tables description? Not a table. I'll put it as a note in certified_type description.

model_designation / module_designation: null — the cert says specs depend on modules used; no explicit module designation. Omit or null.

Model family: models: IT4000E[T], IT6000E[T], IT8000E[T], IT3000M, IT2000M. Labels: maybe family "IT x000E/M"? No explicit family name. family_name null.

Model_level characteristics: none with concrete values. So characteristics.type_level only accuracy_class. Actually should I even include characteristics? I can include type_level accuracy_class.

So "R76". Amendment: null — omit? Rule 8 says omit if not present. I'll omit amendment or null. I'll omit it... Actually including null is fine but rule says omit. I'll include only present fields. Keep accuracy_classes.

For footnote_markers empty arrays — fine to omit. I'll keep values simple: {"value": "III or IIII", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null}. Hmm, strict shape includes unit_id optional? The shape shows unit_id. I'll include unit_id: null.

Should accuracy_class value be a list? Structured value must be number | {min,max} | string. So string "III or IIII" is acceptable. Good.
